title: The GRPO objective and its KL estimator
goal:
Implement two pieces of Equation 3 for one group of $G$ outputs.

1. `kl_k3(logp, logp_ref)` is the estimator of Equation 4, $\frac{\pi_{ref}}{\pi_\theta} - \log\frac{\pi_{ref}}{\pi_\theta} - 1$, computed from log-probabilities of the sampled tokens. It works elementwise.
2. `grpo_objective(logp_new, logp_old, logp_ref, adv, mask, eps, beta)` returns the value of the objective for the group (the quantity to maximize, without the outer expectation over questions). Per token, it takes $\min(r\hat A,\ \operatorname{clip}(r, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon)\hat A)$ with $r = \pi_\theta/\pi_{\theta_{old}}$ and subtracts $\beta$ times the KL estimate. It then averages the tokens of each output with $1/|o_i|$, and averages over the $G$ outputs with $1/G$.

The arrays `logp_new`, `logp_old`, and `logp_ref` have shape `(G, T)`. `adv` has shape `(G,)`: outcome supervision gives every token of output $i$ the same $\hat A_i$. `mask` has shape `(G, T)` and is 1 for real tokens and 0 for padding, so $|o_i|$ is the row sum of the mask.
hints: With `d = logp_ref - logp`, the estimator is `np.exp(d) - d - 1`. Swapping the arguments gives a different, also non-negative number, so the tests check the direction.
The ratio is `np.exp(logp_new - logp_old)`. Broadcast the advantage with `adv[:, None]` so it multiplies every token of its row.
Sum each row over its real tokens, `(per_token * mask).sum(axis=1)`, divide by `mask.sum(axis=1)`, and only then take the mean over rows. One global mean over all tokens weights long outputs more.
The KL term sits inside the per-token bracket and is not part of `adv`. That separation is the paper's point about Equation 3.
